transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-15 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marta (Aperture - Head of Platform), Eli (Aperture - ML Eng), Sana (Aperture - CTO)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping focused on integration approach: use Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDKs, support function/tool-calling for structured outputs, confirm success criteria (latency, cost, accuracy), define workload sizing and benchmark plan, and agree timeline for pilot and engineering handoff.

Topics:
- POC goals and success criteria
- Workload sizing (requests/s, tokens/request, concurrency)
- Benchmarks and metrics (p50/p95 latency, throughput, cost/unit)
- Integration plan: SDKs (Python/Node), OpenAI-compatible API shape, function calling / tool calls, structured JSON outputs and schema validation
- Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC/private deployment options
- Next steps and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Jared: hi everyone, thanks for joining, do we have everything on the agenda?
[00:08] Marta: yep thanks, we'll keep to the top items — focus on integration and what success looks like, we have limited eng cycles so want a tight plan.
[00:15] Priya: great, I can walk through the integration options — Redwood supports our hosted API and can be run dedicated or private if needed, and the endpoints are OpenAI-compatible which usually makes integration easier.
[00:28] Eli: openai-compat is huge for us, we already have some tooling around the OpenAI SDKs. couple questions: function calling? structured JSON output? and how strict is schema enforcement?
[00:40] Priya: yes, function/tool calling is supported, you can define the function signature and Redwood will return structured output we can validate client-side. we also support optional strict JSON mode for models that can reliably output schemas, though we advise adding a lightweight validator in your app.
[00:58] Sana: on success criteria — we care about accuracy on entity extraction (~95 over our labeled set), p50 latency under 200ms for short queries, p95 under 600ms, and cost under $0.01 per inference on average.
[01:15] Jared: good to capture that. we'll propose benchmarks to measure those metrics. Priya, can you outline how we size the workload?
[01:23] Priya: sure — rough numbers from Marta earlier: peak 50 req/s, average 12 req/s, tokens per request usually 400-1,200, some long docs up to 3k tokens but most are shorter. concurrency will be spiky during batch ingest. for embeddings vs generative calls we'll separate the POC scope to start with the generative extraction path.
[01:42] Eli: ok that matches. our current OpenAI usage is about 30k tokens/day but for POC we plan to simulate 200k tokens/day to stress test.
[01:51] Priya: perfect — we'll run two benchmarks: one steady-state at your avg load and one spike test to 60-70 req/s for 5-10 minutes. we'll run these on Redwood hosted first and then on Dedicated to compare cost/latency.
[02:05] Marta: timeline? we want pilot in early July. is that realistic?
[02:10] Jared: if we get SOW signed this week and sample data this Friday, we can start benchmarks next week and aim for initial pilot by 2026-07-06.
[02:19] Priya: engineering tasks for integration: SDK integration (Python + Node examples), create a small client wrapper for function calls and structured output, sample schema for extraction outputs, and test harness for load tests. total eng effort estimated 3-5 days on Aperture side for initial integration.
[02:38] Eli: our stack is Python (FastAPI) and a Node-based ingestion pipeline. do you have example SDKs and quickstart templates?
[02:45] Priya: yes — we'll share Redwood SDK snippets for Python and Node, example code for OpenAI-compatible endpoints (the same request/response shapes), and a function-calling example. they include streaming responses and chunked token handling for long outputs.
[02:58] Marta: how do we handle retries and rate limits? we have internal backoff logic but want recommended practices.
[03:04] Priya: Redwood has client-level retry guidance. for P50-sensitive flows we recommend synchronous calls with small timeouts; for more tolerant flows use streaming and prefix caching. also we provide per-route token and request quotas you can configure.
[03:18] Sana: security is a must — SOC2 in place? KMS for keys? can we run in our VPC?
[03:24] Jared: Redwood's hosted API is SOC2 compliant, we support customer-managed KMS and Private deployment (VPC) options for production. for POC we usually start on hosted with encryption at rest and in transit; if you need VPC we'll scope Dedicated/Private soon after pilot.
[03:41] Eli: for the private deployment do we need to provision hardware or do you provide an appliance?
[03:44] Priya: we offer both a cloud VPC control plane option and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments — we'll share the deployment guide. for the POC, hosted or dedicated are faster.
[03:56] Marta: benchmarks — what metrics will you provide?
[04:00] Priya: we'll provide p50/p95 latency, throughput, token-per-second efficiency, cost per 1k tokens, and qualitative notes on output fidelity. we'll run comparison across model flavors (base, quantized, and any Redwood-verified variants) and GPU types.
[04:18] Eli: do you support function-calling with nested objects? our schema sometimes needs nested arrays for entities.
[04:24] Priya: yes, function schema supports nested objects and arrays. we recommend keeping a canonical JSON schema and a small post-processor to normalize minor variations (common in NLU outputs).
[04:37] Jared: on the OpenAI-compat endpoint — what's the exact surface?
[04:40] Priya: same parameters: model, messages/prompts, temperature, max_tokens, and functions for tool calling. it's intentionally aligned with OpenAI so you can swap SDK code with minimal changes. we also expose batch embeddings and streaming chunked responses.
[04:57] Eli: great. about structured output: any way to enforce required fields strictly on the model side? we've had hallucinated missing fields before.
[05:05] Priya: model-side strict enforcement is model-dependent — some newer variants are much better at schema conformance. Redwood has a strict-json option that runs additional assembly/validator heuristics; still, defense-in-depth is recommended: validator in your app, example driven prompts, and a small set of canonical tests.
[05:23] Marta: can we do a sample run on our data? we'll share a small labeled set, can you return accuracy metrics?
[05:29] Priya: yes we'll run an eval harness on your labeled set and return precision/recall and false-positive/false-negative breakdowns. that's part of the benchmark plan.
[05:39] Jared: ok let's capture acceptance criteria explicitly: 95% entity extraction F1 on the labeled set, p50 latency <200ms, p95 <600ms, cost per inference under target, and ability to integrate via your Python SDK with function-calling and validated JSON output.
[05:58] Sana: agreed. any blockers on data privacy? we need logs retained for 30 days and audit trails for requests.
[06:05] Jared: Redwood provides audit logs, configurable retention for enterprise; for POC we'll enable 30-day retention. keys via customer-managed KMS if required.
[06:17] Eli: on the invoicing/contract side, what does the POC pricing look like?
[06:21] Jared: typical POC credit-based pricing — we'll send a draft SOW with estimated committed tokens and optional conversion to Dedicated if you want predictable capacity. I'll include both hosted and Dedicated cost projections.
[06:33] Priya: technical corner — streaming and partial outputs: if you stream tokens you may need to handle partial JSON assembly; our SDKs include helpers to reassemble stream chunks and validate incrementally.
[06:47] Eli: nice, that saves time. also do you support function calls that trigger external tools, like a database lookup?
[06:53] Priya: yes — the function calling model returns the structured call request; your app executes it and returns the result back as a follow-up message. we can also wire Redwood tool integrations for common connectors, but for POC we'll do app-side tool execution.
[07:06] Marta: what's the recommended model family? we need a balance of cost vs fidelity.
[07:11] Priya: we'll recommend a mid-tier model variant for POC — higher quality than distilled models but more cost-effective than the largest sizes. we'll include quantized variants in the benchmark to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[07:26] Eli: for throughput testing, can you run tests from our region? we care about regional latency.
[07:31] Priya: yes we'll target your region and include cross-region fallbacks in the plan. smart routing can fall back to a compatible variant in a different region if needed.
[07:45] Jared: ok let's go over the benchmark plan in bullets — Priya?
[07:49] Priya: benchmark plan:
- baseline functional test against labeled set (accuracy metrics)
- steady-state perf at average load (12 req/s) measuring p50/p95 and cost
- spike test to 60-70 req/s for short durations to confirm autoscaling and tail latency
- compare hosted vs Dedicated in terms of latency and token cost
- schema conformance tests for function outputs (strict-json pass rate)
- run a streaming test for long docs (3k tokens) to validate reassembly and memory usage

[08:22] Eli: sounds thorough. can you also measure tokenization differences vs our current provider? token counts affect cost.
[08:29] Priya: yes included — we'll provide tokenization delta and recommended prompt engineering to reduce cost.
[08:36] Marta: timeline recap?
[08:39] Jared: SOW and pricing to Aperture by 2026-06-18, Aperture shares sample data by 2026-06-19, Priya to run initial benchmarks 6/22-6/26, results and evaluation meeting 6/29, pilot start ~7/6.
[08:54] Sana: who is the internal owner from Redwood during the POC?
[08:58] Jared: Priya will be the SE lead, I'll manage the commercial side. Priya will pair with Eli for the benchmarks.
[09:06] Eli: small technical Q: do you support KV cache / prefix cache? some queries reuse context heavily.
[09:12] Priya: yes Redwood supports KV cache for repeated contexts and prefix caching to avoid re-sending large static context, that reduces tokens/cost significantly. we'll demo how that works in the test harness.
[09:25] Marta: excellent. any notable risks?
[09:28] Priya: potential risks: schema hallucination on edge cases, longer tail latency under very large spikes (we'll measure), and any enterprise-only compliance items if you need on-prem for production. mitigation: validator, canary rollouts, and Dedicated/private path if needed.
[09:45] Jared: ok final check — deliverables: SOW, SDK + quickstart, benchmark scripts, and security docs. who owns the security docs?
[09:54] Jared: I'll attach our SOC2 report and Priya will send the private deployment checklist and KMS integration docs.
[10:03] Marta: perfect. last question — can we get a demo of the SDK in a 30-min call next week?
[10:08] Priya: yes, let's schedule a 30-min engineering demo — I'll show Python/Node snippets, streaming reassembly, and function-calling flow.
[10:16] Jared: thanks everyone — recap next steps in an email and we'll follow up with SOW.
[10:20] Marta: thanks all.
